'''Martin James Heeney''' (born April 1973) is a professor of chemistry at [[King Abdullah University of Science and Technology]] and professor of Organic Materials  at [[Imperial College London]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Martin Heeney |url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/m.heeney |website=[[Imperial College London]] |access-date=28 June 2021}}</ref>

Heeney is a graduate of [[University of East Anglia]], and received his PhD in organic materials chemistry from the same institution in 1999 under the supervision of Michael Cook.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Martin Heeney Speaks at TOSCA/ORaCEL joint meeting on 3/16/2021 |url=https://labs.sciences.ncsu.edu/oracel/2021/03/10/prof-martin-heeney-speaks-at-tosca-oracel-joint-meeting-on-3-16-2021/ |website=[[North Carolina State University]] |access-date=28 June 2021}}</ref>

He was awarded the [[Corday–Morgan Prize]] by the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=Corday-Morgan Prizes - Previous winners |url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/find-a-prize/corday-morgan-prizes/previous-winners/ |website=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]] |access-date=28 June 2021}}</ref>

He has an [[h-index]] of 98 according to [[Google Scholar]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Martin Heeney |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=rZFqBLEAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao |website=[[Google Scholar]] |access-date=13 November 2023}}</ref>
